claims: In a perigee raise maneuver, a spacecraft fires its engines at apogee to raise perigee.
Apogee is the highest point of an orbit.
Perigee is the lowest point of an orbit.
The NASA Artemis II mission's crewed Orion spacecraft requires a 100-mile (roughly 160-185 km) altitude orbit.
The Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage (ICPS) performs a perigee raise burn approximately 49 minutes after launch.
The ICPS performs the perigee raise burn to bring the Orion capsule into a stable orbit.
The ICPS perigee raise burn reduces the risk of re-entering the Earth's atmosphere too early.
To raise the perigee, the spacecraft must perform a prograde burn at the apogee.
Increasing speed at apogee increases the altitude at the opposite side of the orbit.
The ICPS performs an initial perigee raise to over 100 miles.
The ICPS initial perigee raise is followed by an additional burn to further optimize the orbit for future maneuvers.
The perigee raise maneuver completes the transition from a highly elliptical "park" orbit to a circular or more stable elliptical orbit.
